predecessors.note: The Nawab of Bhopal page has the state "under the Mughal Empire from 1707 to 1737"; Dost Mohammad Khan was "a Pashtun soldier in the Mughal army". The Bhopal State infobox names the Maratha Empire as predecessor, which the text does not support for 1707 (the Marathas appear from 1737).

correction.text: the Bhopal State of 17,876 km2 (1901): the present-day Bhopal, Raisen and Sehore districts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives the 1901 area 17,876 km2 and says "Bhopal state included the present-day Bhopal, Raisen, and Sehore districts"; a box of 1.6 by 0.9 degrees (about 17,300 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years. The extent before 1901 is unknown: Dost Mohammad Khan took only the lease of the Berasia estate in 1709 and the Nizam forced a cession of "much of his territory" in March 1724, neither of which has a boundary on any page opened, so the shape is the late state throughout (an over-estimate for the early years, flagged soft). Overlaps the Mughal and later Maratha shapes of Malwa.

region.text: the first lands of Dost Mohammad Khan about Bhopal and Berasia (a reading; the page gives no extent for 1707)

ledger.note: 1707: Dost Mohammad Khan founds Bhopal State. "The state was founded in 1707" by Dost Mohammad Khan, "a Pashtun soldier in the Mughal army" (infobox Established 1707; the Nawab of Bhopal page: he "founded the state of Bhopal in 1707 and ruled it until 1728"). The page gives no land with the date, so the region is a reading.

1709: Dost Mohammad Khan takes the lease of the Berasia estate. "In 1709, he took on the lease of the Berasia estate." The page does not say from whom (the counterpart is my reading) or the extent; the circle is a reading about Berasia.
1728: the capital moves from Bhopal to Islamnagar. Infobox: "Bhopal (1707-1728 and 1742-1949); Islamnagar (1728-1742)".
1742: the capital returns from Islamnagar to Bhopal. Infobox: "Bhopal (1707-1728 and 1742-1949); Islamnagar (1728-1742)".

region.text: the Bhopal State of 17,876 km2 (1901): the present-day Bhopal, Raisen and Sehore districts

ledger.note: 1 June 1949: the Union Government of India takes over Bhopal. "the Nawab Bhopal had to sign the agreement for merger on 30 April 1949"; "taken over by the Union Government of India on 1 June 1949"; infobox Disestablished 1 June 1949. The state was "independent from 1947 to 1949" on the page (it "expressed his wish to retain Bhopal as a separate independent state in March 1948"). The page lists a successor Bhopal State (1949-1956) without dating its end.

wars.name: Battle of Bhopal
wars.outcome: On 24 December 1737 Baji Rao beat the Mughal forces under Nizam-ul-Mulk, with the Nawab of Bhopal among the vassal belligerents; the peace of 7 January 1738 (Treaty of Bhopal, signed at Doraha) gave the Marathas Malwa and 50 lakh rupees; the page is silent on any Bhopal territory lost.
wars.note: Battle of Bhopal page: "fought on 24 December 1737 in Bhopal"; "on 7 January 1738, a peace treaty was signed" between Peshwa Bajirao and Jai Singh II at Doraha; "Mughals cede large territory of Malwa (central India) to Marathas". Bhopal State page: the state was a Maratha-era state 1737-1818. The maratha-empire dossier should record the vassal_start for bhopal-state from 1737 to 1818.

wars.name: Nizam-ul-Mulk invasion of Bhopal
wars.outcome: The Nizam invaded in March 1724 and forced Dost Mohammad Khan to cede much of his territory.
wars.note: Bhopal State page: Nizam-ul-Mulk "invaded Bhopal in March 1724, forcing Khan to cede much of his territory"; the state "came under the suzerainty of the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1723". No land is named, so the cession is not a ledger event (a loss needs a region) and the shape is not changed; the hyderabad-state dossier should carry the vassal_start from 1723.

certainty.note: The pages give the 1901 area and the three districts only; the shape is a box of that area for all years.

sources.title: Bhopal State
sources.note: Established 1707; Berasia lease 1709; Nizam suzerainty 1723; March 1724 cession; Battle of Bhopal 1737; Anglo-Bhopal treaty 1818; begums 1819-1926; area 17,876 km2; merger agreement 30 April 1949, takeover 1 June 1949.

sources.title: Battle of Bhopal
sources.note: 24 December 1737, Baji Rao against the Mughals under Nizam-ul-Mulk; treaty of 7 January 1738 at Doraha; Mughals cede Malwa; silent on Bhopal territory.

sources.title: Nawab of Bhopal
sources.note: Founded 1707 by Dost Muhammad Khan; Islamnagar founded 1716 and early 1720s; Mughal period 1707-1737, Maratha 1737-1818, British 1818-1947; ruler list; silent on territory.

notes: Three pages opened (Bhopal State, Battle of Bhopal, Nawab of Bhopal). Fetches of Dost Mohammad Khan (Bhopal) and (Nawab of Bhopal) returned url_not_found; Qudsia Begum returned a different (Delhi) person and is not cited. The pages give no boundary at any date; the early extent (Berasia lease 1709, Nizam cession March 1724 of "much of his territory") and the later growth to 17,876 km2 are not on the pages opened. Conflicts: infobox predecessor Maratha Empire against the text (Mughal 1707-1737, Maratha 1737-1818); Sikandar and Shah Jahan Begum reign years (list against text); Hamidullah Khan 1926-1949 (infobox) against 1926-1947 (Nawab page). Vassal records for the suzerains: Nizam of Hyderabad from 1723 (hyderabad-state), Maratha confederacy 1737-1818 (maratha-empire), the East India Company from the Anglo-Bhopal treaty of February-March 1818 to 1947 (british-empire / british-raj). Bhopal State (1949-1956) is a successor entity the page names and does not date; the Part C state needs a dossier or umbrella from the post-1947 group.
